Smart-Camera-Integration:2.source: Smart Camera is a standalone local-player view service. Your mod registers a friendly name and stable namespaced string view IDs, then supplies a world frame or an absolute camera pose. Registration is separate from rendering and from saved player overrides. Idle views remain discoverable; deactivate until a subject is ready and unregister on owner/world teardown.

Smart-Camera-Integration:3.source: The [full API guide](https://github.com/majormer/SmartCamera/blob/master/SMARTCAMERA_API_INTEGRATION.md) covers optional plugin/module dependencies, feature discovery, code examples, ownership, multiple views, settings ranges, save scope, lifecycle and migration. The [complete Space Elevator Camera plugin](https://github.com/majormer/SmartCamera/tree/master/docs/examples/SpaceElevatorCamera) is included as a tested source reference, with its own player-look controls and no SmartFoundations dependency.

Smart-Camera:1.source: > **Unreleased draft.** Prepared for the coordinated Smart! 35.0.0 release. This candidate is not compatible with the current Smart! package on SMR. Smart Camera can work by itself; the coordinated Smart! version is 35.0.0.

Smart-Camera:2.source: Smart Camera gives you additional views while building. It follows a normal hologram without Smart!, accepts Smart's grid/frontier framing when a compatible Smart! is engaged, and lets other mods supply independent camera views. It does not change placement permissions, resource costs or your world's buildable data.

Smart-Camera:4.source:
1. Load a game and select an ordinary buildable with the build gun. The built-in view follows that hologram; conveyor lifts use their endpoint view.
2. With a compatible Smart! installed and engaged, Smart supplies its build-preview view. Equivalent default/Smart views do not appear twice.
3. Open **Mods → Smart! Camera** to configure the built-in view and registered cameras. Other mods' friendly names/cameras appear automatically after they register in the loaded world; no typed IDs or manual profile are required.
4. Disable **Built-in build gun view** if you only want cameras supplied by other mods. Registered views have separate Enabled controls.

Smart-Camera:31.source: ### Built-in view with Smart! assistance off

Smart-Camera:32.source: ![Smart Camera’s built-in view follows a single Large Fan hologram while Smart! building assistance is switched off.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/majormer/SmartFoundations/images/v35/camera-built-in.png)

Smart-Camera:33.source: Smart Camera’s built-in view follows a single Large Fan hologram while Smart! building assistance is switched off.

Smart-Camera:34.source: This example has Smart! installed but its session assistance disabled. The inset is supplied by Smart Camera itself, rather than Smart!’s grid camera. Re-select the building after switching assistance off.

Smart-Camera:6.source:
| Default control | Action |
|---|---|
| `[` | Cycle the active building camera's angle, including Off |
| Hold `]` + mouse wheel | Adjust building-camera distance; scroll up moves closer, down moves farther |
| `F8` | Enter live layout Edit Mode |
| Drag a viewport's title bar | Move that registered viewport |
| Drag any L-shaped corner | Resize that registered viewport |
| **Done / Lock** | Save pending layout changes and return to building |

Smart-Camera:7.source: Rebind the three Camera actions in the native **Options → Keybindings → Smart! Camera Controls** section. These controls do not require a numpad. Outside Edit Mode, the viewport does not intercept ordinary building clicks. Mods that supply absolute camera poses own their aiming controls; Camera's build-angle/zoom keys do not replace them.

Smart-Camera:9.source: Building modes are **Left45, Front45, Right45, Back45, TopDown, ForwardLevel** and lift-only **Periscope**; **Off** hides the building view. Periscope looks outward from the selected conveyor-lift endpoint, helping you check its direction and alignment while setting height. It is skipped when cycling an ordinary non-lift preview. Adjustable building-camera distance is 5–50m.

Smart-Camera:10.source: An explicit angle override can replace automatic lift framing. To restore automatic behavior without losing your layout, choose **Use mod framing and distance** in the all-saves angle menu, or **Use global framing and distance** for this save. Changing layout alone preserves inherited framing and distance.

Smart-Camera:12.source: Press **F8** while a view is visible. Each active viewport gets its mod/camera title and four corner handles. Drag to place it where it helps your build; release to finish the preview gesture. Camera position in the world and the hologram's native placement are independent of the overlay's screen rectangle.

Smart-Camera:14.source: The editor uses the last selected **All saves / This save** scope, initially All saves. Choose **All saves / This save** in the editor, or choose the scope in Camera settings before **Edit viewport layout after Resume**. Changing the editor scope keeps your current previews. An explicit All saves edit includes this save and any other existing saved profiles for that camera. Moving or resizing with All saves selected updates its position and size across those profiles. Other settings, such as brightness or Enabled, keep their own values. Choose This save to change the layout only for this world. Press **Done / Lock** to save all pending edits, or **Cancel** / Escape to discard them. When Smart! is installed, the same Done/Lock and Cancel actions also complete its HUD appearance preview; the HUD preferences still apply across saves. Pressing F8 again saves and exits. Inactive views stay in settings, but need an active subject to appear in the live layout editor.

Smart-Camera:16.source: Registered cameras show **Enabled**, **Active/Inactive**, screen X/Y, width/height, scale, update rate and brightness. Applicable building views also show angle and distance. Values apply live and save immediately; no world reload is required.

Smart-Camera:35.source:
| Setting | Meaning and range |
|---|---|
| Position X / Y | Normalized screen position 0–1 from the upper-left corner |
| Width / height | Render-target dimensions 64–2048 pixels per axis |
| Scale | Display scale 0.1–2; effective screen size is dimensions × scale |
| Update rate | 5–60 captures/sec; 20 is the default suggestion |
| Brightness | -3 to +3 EV; positive values brighten the picture. Reduce it if the image looks washed out. |
| Building view distance | 500–5000 cm (5–50m), when the consumer uses building angles |

Smart-Camera:18.source: Start with consumer suggestions, then adjust only what you need. Higher resolutions, update rates and more active views can increase rendering cost.

Smart-Camera:19.source: **All saves** applies the edited field globally and to that camera's existing saved overrides. For example, disabling a camera under All saves disables it in the current world too, even if you previously saved a layout there. Changing brightness does not overwrite saved window positions, and changing position does not re-enable a disabled camera. **This save** edits only the loaded native save's profile; other saves and global values are untouched. Later edits use whichever scope you explicitly choose. Preferences are local to your installation/player; they are not replicated settings for everyone on the server. A save name is not the identity key, so do not rename files to manage Camera profiles.

Smart-Camera:20.source: **Use mod suggestions** under All saves resets that camera's complete profile across all saves, including its saved overrides. **Use global settings** under This save removes only this save's override. Other cameras are unchanged. The framing/distance inheritance option resets only those two controls and preserves layout. Legacy numeric profiles retain their explicit settings until adjusted or reset.

Smart-Camera:22.source: Each mod can register several cameras with stable namespaced string IDs. Friendly mod and camera names are visible even when the view is inactive. A missing subject, disabled view or open native menu can make it inactive without removing its settings entry.

Smart-Camera:23.source: The included **Space Elevator Camera** reference uses `SpaceElevatorCamera:player-look`. Its origin stays above the native Space Elevator; turning the player rotates the view through 360°, and looking up/down changes pitch. Player movement does not translate it. No elevator means no rendered reference view. This is a separate example consumer, not a built-in Camera behavior or a dependency on Smart!.

Smart-Camera:36.source: ![The layout editor shows two independent views: Smart!’s build preview and Space Elevator Camera. Their title bars and corner handles identify the views being edited.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/majormer/SmartFoundations/images/v35/camera-multiple-views.png)

Smart-Camera:37.source: The layout editor shows two independent views: Smart!’s build preview and Space Elevator Camera. Their title bars and corner handles identify the views being edited.

Smart-Camera:38.source: The small build view keeps the two Fan previews in frame while the independent Space Elevator view looks over a different part of the world. Move and resize each window separately in Edit Mode; **Done / Lock** saves the chosen layout.

Smart-Camera:25.source: Native pause/interaction menus hide the pictures and suspend captures. Resume restores eligible views. Edit Mode is the deliberate exception so you can adjust live rectangles.

Smart-Camera:26.source: Rendering happens on each local client, including standalone and multiplayer clients; a dedicated server does not render these views. Use matching released packages as required by the mod manager. Ordinary saves remain usable without Camera or Smart!.

Smart-Camera:27.source: If no view appears, check the loaded world's registration list, Enabled state, built-in toggle, active subject and angle (Off hides a building view). If lift framing differs from expectations, restore framing/distance inheritance. If a consumer's camera disappears, that mod may no longer have a valid subject. Hardware-specific black-startup and older latest-building reports remain separately tracked; this guide does not promise that every reported graphics/network issue is resolved.

Smart-Camera:28.source: Developers: see the [consumer API guide](Smart-Camera-Integration) and [complete reference plugin](https://github.com/majormer/SmartCamera/tree/master/docs/examples/SpaceElevatorCamera).

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:1.source: Press **K** with a supported buildable selected. Smart's tools share one window, with the controls that apply to your current building.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:4.source:
| Tab | Use it to |
|---|---|
| **Scaling** | Repeat the held building and edit its grid, spacing, steps, stagger and rotation |
| **Extend** | Select an existing matching factory module, inspect captured companions and repeat it |
| **Walking** | Steer a connected route, or resume a compatible existing bus |
| **Upgrade** | Scan existing infrastructure, choose a tier and review replacement costs |
| **Restore** | Save/load Grid Presets or captured Modules |

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:5.source: Available tasks follow the held building. Railway tracks and Vehicle Paths open Walking directly and do not offer ordinary Scaling. A raw pipe recipe can open Upgrade; to start or resume a pipe walk, equip the matching **stackable support** first.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:6.source: Switching to Upgrade suspends an active walk. Switching to a task that would discard an unbuilt path asks for confirmation. Read the warning before continuing; declining keeps the path.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:8.source: Scaling keeps X/Y/Z in aligned columns. These fields stay building-relative even with Player Relative controls enabled. The colored arrows show the actual directions.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:9.source: **Apply placement immediately** controls placement geometry. When off, edit the grid and transforms, then press **Apply** to update the world preview. Apply does not construct anything. Closing discards unapplied placement edits. **Reset** resets the placement controls.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:10.source: Connection preferences, production recipes and the applicable native building controls are **live settings**. For example, changing pipe routing rebuilds its preview immediately; wall-support rotation changes the support itself. They are labeled separately and are not waiting for the placement Apply button. Check the preview and material quote before firing the build gun.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:12.source: Hover a small **?** button beside a building or section label for help. Click to keep the details expanded; click again to collapse them. Each task explains its own workflow.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:13.source: Drag the title bar with the left mouse button, or use the existing right-button drag gesture. A manually moved panel remembers its position across saves. The mod settings offer a position reset.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:15.source: The HUD shows the active value, colored grid counts and relevant control hints. **Controls: Building Relative** or **Controls: Player Relative** identifies how the wheel and directional keys behave. The label describes controls, not the selected visual theme.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:16.source: During Walking the HUD identifies the route family and current segment. Hints change to route operations such as advancing, turning and climbing. Remapped controls are reflected in the hints.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:17.source: ![Shared HUD and Camera editor with a single Done / Lock action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/majormer/SmartFoundations/images/v35/layout-editor.png)

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:19.source: Enter layout **Edit Mode** with **F8** by default, or choose **Edit HUD layout after Resume** in mod settings. Drag the HUD title bar to move it and use its resize handle or Scale field to change its size. Choose from the six themes; the existing multilingual font family is retained.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:20.source: With Smart Camera installed, the same edit session includes the camera windows. **Done / Lock** saves pending HUD and camera layout edits together. **Cancel** or Escape discards the pending edits. Normal building input and the ordinary scaling HUD return when the editor closes.

Smart-Panel-and-HUD:21.source: HUD appearance and panel positions apply **across all saves on your installation**. The Camera editor's All saves / This save selector applies to camera preferences only. **Reset HUD Appearance** restores the HUD defaults. Outside Edit Mode the HUD is locked and does not intercept building clicks.

Smart-Restore:1.source: Smart Restore saves your Smart! work so you can reuse it later, share it, or stamp a whole factory module out again the same way every time. Open **K → Restore** in the shared [Smart Panel](Smart-Panel-and-HUD). Its two subtabs are **Grid Presets** and **Modules**.

Smart-Restore:2.source: It is the answer to "I spent ages dialing in this layout — how do I get it back?"

Smart-Restore:3.source: ![Restore task with Grid Presets and Modules subtabs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/majormer/SmartFoundations/images/v35/restore.png)

Smart-Restore:5.source: A Grid Preset saves everything you set up in the Smart Panel, as a named preset you can load back with one click:

Smart-Restore:6.source:
- Grid size (X, Y, Z).
- Spacing, Steps, Stagger, and Rotation.
- The building and its selected production recipe.
- Auto-Connect settings.

Smart-Restore:7.source: Use the Grid Presets tab to:

Smart-Restore:8.source:
- **Save from Panel** — name your current panel setup and save it as a preset.
- **Load to Panel** — load a saved preset back into the panel to fine-tune before building, or apply it as-is.
- **Export Code / Import Code** — share a preset as a code, or load one someone shared with you.

Smart-Restore:9.source: Each preset shows a plain-language summary of what it holds (building, grid, transforms, recipe) so you can tell them apart at a glance.

Smart-Restore:11.source: A Module captures a whole **Extend manifold** — a wired unit of buildings with their belts, pipes, lifts, distributors, and power — that you can stamp down repeatedly.

Smart-Restore:12.source:
- After you preview or build a Smart [Extend](Extend), it lands in the **Extend clipboard** at the top of the tab. **Save as Module** turns that captured layout into a named, reusable Module.
- **Load Module** for a saved Module to rebuild that layout: equip its source building and it becomes a live preview you can **stamp** (fire to place, repeatedly) and **scroll to scale** on the fly.
- Because a restored Module isn't locked to one side the way a fresh Scaled Extend is, you can **rescale the run in either direction** along its axis before placing — scroll one way to grow it one way, the other way to grow it the other.
- **Export Code / Import Code** share Modules the same way presets do.

Smart-Restore:13.source: Each Module shows a summary of its parts (how many belts, pipes, distributors, and so on) so you know what it rebuilds.

Smart-Restore:30.source: ![The Modules tab shows a captured Constructor layout and its matching saved entry beside the source buildings.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/majormer/SmartFoundations/images/v35/saved-modules-constructor.png)

Smart-Restore:31.source: The Modules tab shows a captured Constructor layout and its matching saved entry beside the source buildings.

Smart-Restore:15.source: Use **Grid Z** to repeat the saved module on additional floors, and **Z spacing** to adjust the floor interval. Each layer rebuilds its captured factories and infrastructure with normal material costs.

Smart-Restore:16.source: Saving after a scaled Extend captures **one complete module**, so it can be repeated again in Restore. If an older module contains extra poles/cables or cannot identify its cable endpoints, recapture it from a working layout. Existing saved layouts are not rewritten automatically.

Smart-Restore:17.source: Pipe floor holes retain their captured top and bottom attachments on the correct floor. Power cables preserve each outlet face and its available slots. A cable beyond the normal game range makes the Restore preview invalid; reduce spacing or adjust the layout before building. A changed source layout or material quote can also require selecting the source again.

Smart-Restore:18.source: Water Extractor Modules remain horizontal and validate water depth and terrain for every child. Associated route supports retain their captured placement. Restore does not enable arbitrary cloning of another mod's factory buildings.

Smart-Restore:19.source: **Load to Panel** loads editable placement values; it does not construct a saved grid. **Load Module** arms a captured layout for placement. Read the selected entry's summary and material quote before building.

Smart-Restore:21.source: Use **K → Restore** to save, select, load, import or export layouts. After loading, use the Scaling Panel or wheel/numpad controls to adjust the placement; the HUD reports the resulting grid and active adjustment. Fire the build gun to construct it at the displayed cost.

Smart-Restore:22.source: To cycle recently applied restores without reopening the Panel, hold `U` and press `Num 9` for the next recent preset or `Num 3` to step back. See [Controls](Controls).

Smart-Restore:24.source: Shared presets and Modules are checked against your current unlocks before they can be imported or applied. If one needs a building, recipe, belt or pipe tier, lift, splitter, merger, power component, or other piece you have not unlocked yet, Smart! rejects it instead of letting you build something you could not place by hand.

Smart-Restore:25.source: That keeps shared setups honest: importing one never skips progression.

Smart-Restore:27.source:
- [Extend](Extend) — the feature whose manifolds the Modules tab captures.
- [Smart Panel and HUD](Smart-Panel-and-HUD) — where the Restore tab lives.
- [Grid Scaling](Grid-Scaling) and [Transforms](Transforms) — what a Grid Preset saves.

Smart-Upgrade:1.source: Smart Upgrade helps replace older infrastructure after you unlock better tiers.

Smart-Upgrade:2.source: Use it when you want to upgrade many belts, lifts, pipes, or power poles without replacing each one by hand.

Smart-Upgrade:4.source:
| Type | Supported |
|------|-----------|
| Conveyor belts | Yes, Mk1-Mk6 |
| Conveyor lifts | Yes, Mk1-Mk6 |
| Pipes | Yes, Mk1-Mk2 |
| Power poles | Yes, Mk1-Mk3 |
| Wall outlets | Yes, Mk1-Mk3 |
| Miners | Upgrade only; retain the native resource node |
| Power towers | Scan/traversal context only |

Smart-Upgrade:6.source:
1. Open **K → Upgrade** with a supported building held. Belts, pipes and wire/power lines can open this task directly.
2. Choose a scan mode.
3. Scan nearby items or a connected network.
4. Pick the family and target tier — and, on a network scan, optionally a single source tier to upgrade just that tier.
5. Review the material cost.
6. Run the upgrade.

Smart-Upgrade:7.source: Power poles and wall outlets still open the normal Smart Panel when held so they can be scaled. To upgrade them, open Smart Upgrade from a wire/power line or use scan modes.

Smart-Upgrade:10.source:
- A radius around you.
- The whole map by using radius `0`.
- A connected network starting from an anchor buildable.

Smart-Upgrade:11.source: Network traversal is useful when you want to upgrade one belt line, pipe line, or power network without touching unrelated nearby items. For **Network**, press **Select Target**, then click the intended buildable in the world outside the Panel. The Panel itself does not pass clicks through. One target click finishes selection; Escape cancels it. An invalid hit keeps the previous target. Selecting a new target clears the old scan and quote, so scan again before upgrading. The held tier does not choose the target network. Traversal follows pipes through cross and T junctions and refreshes after an upgrade.

Smart-Upgrade:13.source: A network scan lists the tiers it found in the connected run, and lets you choose which to upgrade:

Smart-Upgrade:14.source:
- Click a specific tier — for example **Mk.2** — to upgrade **only** that tier to your target. Bump your Mk.2 belts to Mk.3 and leave the Mk.4s untouched.
- Pick **All tiers** to bring every differing belt, lift, or pipe tier to the selected target. This can upgrade some tiers and downgrade others in the same run.

Smart-Upgrade:15.source: This matches the tier control the radius scan already had.

Smart-Upgrade:17.source: Choose a lower unlocked target tier to downgrade belts, conveyor lifts, or pipes. A specific source-tier row changes only that tier; **All tiers** changes every differing logistics tier in the selected network.

Smart-Upgrade:18.source: Power poles and wall outlets remain upgrade-only, including in an All tiers selection. Downgrades use the same replacement-cost and refund accounting below.

Smart-Upgrade:20.source: Smart Upgrade calculates the cost of the new item and subtracts the refund from the old item. It uses your inventory and central storage according to your normal preferences.

Smart-Upgrade:21.source: If there is overflow from refunds, Smart! can spawn a dismantle crate near you.

Smart-Upgrade:23.source: **Preserve dismantle groups** is on by default. Supported replacements retain their original Smart group, including groups with only one building. Native Designer ownership is retained inside a Blueprint Designer. Turning the option off skips Smart's membership transfer; it does not strip membership already preserved by native replacement.

Smart-Upgrade:24.source: Miners and power/capacity families are upgrade-only. Logistics downgrades remain available for belts, lifts and pipes. A rejected replacement or insufficient resources leaves the original in place.

Smart-Upgrade:26.source: Large conveyor upgrades are complicated because Satisfactory groups belts and lifts into conveyor chain actors internally. Smart! includes stabilization and diagnostics, but very large upgrades may still need a save/reload if the game reports unsettled chain state afterward.

Smart-Walking:1.source: Walking creates a connected route one segment at a time. Use it for conveyor buses, pipes, Hypertubes, railway tracks and Vehicle Paths. It previews the route before building and charges normal materials for new construction.

Smart-Walking:2.source: ![Three-lane pipe walk with a turn and rise on a clear platform](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/majormer/SmartFoundations/images/v35/walking-bus.png)

Smart-Walking:4.source:
1. Equip a **Stackable Conveyor Pole**, **Stackable Pipeline Support** or **Stackable Hypertube Support** for that family. For rails or Vehicle Paths, select the corresponding native buildable.
2. Aim at a valid starting placement, then open **K → Walking**. Route-only buildables open this task directly.
3. Add and steer segments. Review the whole preview, then fire the build gun to construct it.

Smart-Walking:6.source: Holding a pipe or belt alone is not the entry point. **Equip the matching stackable support**, even when you want to continue from an existing pipe or belt.

Smart-Walking:7.source:
1. Close the Panel and equip that support.
2. Aim at an **open endpoint** of the existing line, or its compatible stackable support at the endpoint.
3. Open **K → Walking** without placing a new starting support.
4. Check the **Resume** summary: lanes, levels and spacing should describe the bus you intended to continue.
5. Advance the new route and inspect the connections before building.

Smart-Walking:8.source: Smart can recognize a regular cross-section such as four side-by-side lines, a 3×3 bus, or a compatible manually placed grid. The start must be horizontal and the endpoints must be open and unambiguous. Wall/floor attachments are excluded. An occupied endpoint or irregular arrangement is not a valid resume target. The continuation can climb after the horizontal start.

Smart-Walking:9.source: Existing lines and supports remain in place; only new construction is charged.

Smart-Walking:11.source: Increase the resumed bus's lane or level count to add more lines. For example, resume four lanes and grow to six: the original four stay intact, while Smart supplies the missing starting supports and new route pieces for the added lanes. Expansion is not limited to two additional lanes.

Smart-Walking:12.source: After building, resume from the open start of an added lane and walk backward toward its source. Conveyor flow is preserved per lane, including buses whose belts run in opposite directions. Inspect the flow arrows; reversing the direction you walk must not reverse an existing belt's transport direction.

Smart-Walking:14.source:
| Control | Walking operation |
|---|---|
| Advance / Scale X | Add a segment; decrease to remove the last segment |
| Scale Y / Z | Adjust bus lanes / levels where supported |
| Spacing | Segment advance distance |
| Rotation | Turn |
| Steps | Rise or descend |
| Stagger | Shift sideways |

Smart-Walking:15.source: See [Controls](Controls) for defaults. Walking is **segment-relative**; Player Relative scaling does not change these route meanings. Smart Camera can follow the leading segment while you remain at the start.

Smart-Walking:16.source: The Walking tab lists each segment's **Advance, Turn, Rise, Shift** and **Preview exit** heading. Edit an earlier segment to reshape the rest of the preview. With **Apply segment edits immediately** off, the visible values remain staged until Apply. Connection options such as tier, routing and supported flow/style preferences are live and labeled separately.

Smart-Walking:17.source: ![Walking segment table, preview heading and live connection options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/majormer/SmartFoundations/images/v35/walking-segments.png)

Smart-Walking:19.source:
- Belts keep native flow, span and slope restrictions. Use lifts separately where a belt cannot make a climb.
- Pipes and Hypertubes follow their own native routing restrictions. They do not have conveyor-style item flow direction.
- Railway curves use native-style routing and the **100 m maximum applies to the full curved track**, not just the straight distance between endpoints. Shorten a turn or split it into more segments when needed. Separate lines retain separate buffer stops.
- Vehicle Paths are directed routes. Join the appropriate free endpoint and use the correct travel direction. To test a finished route with a vehicle, provide the native station connections, fuel, power and schedule it needs; a visible path alone is not a running transport service.

Smart-Walking:21.source: Fire to commit the new route. Missing materials, stale endpoints or a native-invalid segment prevent construction; correct the preview before trying again. Cancel or holster to discard an unbuilt route. Switching tasks warns when it would lose that route.

Smart-Walking:22.source: Walking previews locally and construction is checked by the authoritative game in multiplayer. Existing route objects remain normal Satisfactory buildings. See [Compatibility and Multiplayer](Compatibility-and-Multiplayer).

Support-Development:1.source: Smart! is a passion project built for the Satisfactory community. Development, testing, documentation, support, and release work all take time.

Support-Development:2.source: Support is completely optional. If Smart! saves you time and you want to help keep development sustainable, Ko-fi contributions are appreciated:

Support-Development:4.source: You can also support Smart! without donating:

Support-Development:5.source:

- Join the [Smart! Discord](https://discord.gg/SgXY4CwXYw) for help, testing discussion, and feedback.
- Share screenshots, videos, and examples of what you build with Smart!.
- Help other players understand the current controls and features.
- Contribute fixes or documentation through pull requests.

Support-Development:6.source: No pressure. Every kind of support helps.

Supported-Buildings:1.source: Smart! uses known building profiles and each buildable's supported features. A single-click vanilla placement does not guarantee Smart scaling, and an unavailable axis is deliberately unavailable through the Panel, keys and presets alike.

Supported-Buildings:3.source:
- Foundations, ramps, walls, roof families and corners, barriers, railings, walkways and catwalks.
- Supported native production buildings, storage and fluid buffers.
- Power poles, outlets, supported generators and power storage.
- Distributors, junctions, pumps, valves, compatible supports and passthroughs.
- [Conveyor Lifts Mk.1–Mk.6](Conveyor-Lift-Grids), retaining selected height, direction and flow.
- Beams/connectors, native pillars/bases, ladders, signs, lights and Jump Pads with their applicable selected state.
- Large Fans and Vents with native mounting; supported roof/corner details.
- FICSMAS Candy Canes, Wreaths, Snowmen, Snow Dispensers, Giant Trees and Snow Cannons when their native seasonal recipes are available.
- Saved [Blueprints](Blueprints), with eligible seam connections.

Supported-Buildings:4.source: Placement retains native restrictions. Wall supports and tilted pillars use their accepted rotation. New fixed-size profiles use native snapping intervals where available, or rounded-up placement intervals; vertical spacing prevents overlap on the applicable native nudge grid.

Supported-Buildings:6.source:
| Building or family | Supported workflow |
|---|---|
| Belts, pipes, Hypertubes | Auto-Connect and Walking; connected parts can accompany supported Extend/Restore modules |
| Railway tracks | Walking and compatible seams between repeated Blueprints; no ordinary track grid scaling |
| Vehicle Paths | Directed Walking and compatible seams between repeated Blueprints |
| [Water Extractors](Water-Extractors) | Horizontal scaling, Extend and Restore; every child validates water depth/terrain |
| Miners | Smart Upgrade on the original resource node; no free-placement grid |
| Elevator assemblies | Copies retain selected height and floor stops; native shaft edits retain the Smart Dismantle group. Floor stops cannot be scaled independently. |

Supported-Buildings:7.source: Train signals, train stations/platforms, Conveyor Monitor grids and Portal Potty are outside this support set. Do not infer support for every building from another mod. Smart does not maintain spacing profiles for all third-party factory buildings; manual spacing may help compatible ordinary grid placements, but does not add Extend support or change native permissions.

Supported-Buildings:9.source: See the [Buildable Gallery](Buildable-Gallery) for selected shapes, native mounting and buildable-specific controls.

Transforms:1.source: Transforms change the shape of a scaled grid. They are what turn a plain row or rectangle into something with gaps, height changes, offsets, or arcs.

Transforms:2.source: ![Spacing, Steps and Stagger values beside the transformed grid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/majormer/SmartFoundations/images/v35/transforms.png)

Transforms:4.source: Open **K → Scaling → Placement** to enter **Spacing (m)**, **Steps (m)**, **Stagger (m)** and **Z stagger (m)** directly in the Smart Panel. Use the **Rotation** row below for the per-copy angle and its X/Y progression selector. The Panel keeps the grid's X/Y/Z axes even with Player Relative controls enabled.

Transforms:5.source: Alternatively, use the modifier keys with the mouse wheel or numpad described below. The runtime HUD shows the active transform, target axis and value while you adjust it; it is not a separate value-entry panel. With **Apply placement immediately** off, Panel geometry edits wait for **Apply**. Applying updates the preview; firing the build gun constructs it.

Transforms:7.source: Spacing adds extra distance between each copy.

Transforms:9.source:
- Machine rows that need belt space.
- Foundations with deliberate gaps.
- Cleaner production layouts.

Transforms:11.source:
- Hold `;`.
- Use `Num 8`, `Num 5`, or mouse wheel.
- Press `Num 0` to switch between X, Y, and Z spacing.

Transforms:13.source: Steps raise or lower each row or column.

Transforms:15.source:
- Stair-step foundation layouts.
- Terraced factories.
- Ramps and decorative structure work.

Transforms:17.source:
- Hold `I`.
- Use `Num 8`, `Num 5`, or mouse wheel.
- Press `Num 0` to switch between X and Y stepping.

Transforms:21.source:
- Diagonal-looking patterns.
- Offset machine rows.
- Leaning or angled multi-layer layouts.

Transforms:23.source:
- Hold `Y`.
- Use `Num 8`, `Num 5`, or mouse wheel.
- Press `Num 0` to toggle between the **Stack** and **Flat** stagger families; re-tap `Y` to switch direction within a family (`Num 9` / `Num 3` jump straight to Stack or Flat).

Transforms:25.source: Rotation places copies around a horizontal arc — each copy is yawed a little more than the last.

Transforms:27.source:
- Curved walls.
- Circular foundation patterns.
- Decorative arcs.

Transforms:29.source:
- Hold `,`.
- Use `Num 8`, `Num 5`, or mouse wheel to set the per-copy angle.
- Press `Num 0` (or use the **X/Y selector on the Rotation row of the Smart! Panel**) to choose which grid axis the rotation builds up along:
  - **X** (default) — the rotation accumulates along the columns, so the **run** curves as it extends.
  - **Y** — the rotation accumulates along the rows, so the **rows** fan out around the vertical instead.

Transforms:30.source: Grid Rotation creates a horizontal yaw arc; it does not add a vertical-arch tool. **Wall rotation** on Pipeline/Hypertube wall supports is a separate native 45° control that turns the support itself, including vertical runs. Native tilted pillars also retain their selected parent frame when repeated.

Troubleshooting:1.source: For broader common questions from Discord and release history, see the [FAQ](FAQ).

Troubleshooting:4.source:
- You are holding the build gun.
- You have an active buildable hologram.
- Smart! controls are still bound under Options > Keybindings > "Smart! Mod Controls".
- You are not typing in a search box or another UI.
- The Smart! mod is enabled.

Troubleshooting:6.source: ## Mouse Wheel Rotates Instead Of Scaling

Troubleshooting:7.source: That is expected when no Smart mode is active. Smart! leaves mouse wheel to vanilla rotation unless you are holding a Smart modifier or mode key.

Troubleshooting:9.source:
- Hold `X` for X.
- Hold `Z` for Y.
- Hold `X + Z` for Z.

Troubleshooting:10.source: To adjust transforms with mouse wheel:

Troubleshooting:11.source:
- Hold `;` for Spacing.
- Hold `I` for Steps.
- Hold `Y` for Stagger.
- Hold `,` for Rotation.

Troubleshooting:13.source: Auto-Connect skips connections when it cannot safely make them.

Troubleshooting:14.source: When this happens, the Smart! HUD shows a short summary while you aim — for example, *"2 belt connection(s) skipped: too steep"* — so you can see that something didn't connect and why. Some Auto-Connect paths omit the invalid connection; workflows that require a complete validated route can block the whole placement. Read the current preview message and quote.

Troubleshooting:15.source: Belts and pipes connect anywhere the game itself would let you place one by hand, so "too steep" or "invalid shape" now only appears when the conveyor or pipe genuinely can't be routed — not just because the connectors are at an awkward angle. If a connection is skipped, it usually means the same manual belt or pipe wouldn't build either.

Troubleshooting:17.source:
- Auto-Connect is disabled.
- The tier setting is not right.
- The connector is **too far** away.
- The belt is **too steep** to build (the game itself would reject the conveyor).
- The belt shape is **invalid** (the routed curve can't be built).
- The connector direction is incompatible.
- A **lane** between distributors couldn't be completed.
- The power pole has no free connection slots.

Troubleshooting:18.source: If a connection is skipped as too steep or too far, moving the grid a little further from the building, or reducing the height offset between levels, usually brings it into range. Try placing a smaller test layout to see which part is confusing the preview.

Troubleshooting:21.source:
- Extend is enabled.
- You are aiming at an existing source building.
- You are holding a matching buildable.
- There is room in the direction Smart! is trying to extend.
- You did not double-tap `Num 0` to disable Smart Auto-Connect and Extend for the session.

Troubleshooting:22.source: ## Smart Upgrade Feels Stuck Or Risky

Troubleshooting:23.source: For large belt and lift upgrades, wait a moment after the upgrade finishes. Conveyor networks can take time to settle.

Troubleshooting:24.source: If diagnostics still look bad after a very large upgrade, save and reload before trying more repair actions.

Troubleshooting:25.source: ## Walking is unavailable while holding a pipe or belt

Troubleshooting:26.source: Close the Panel, equip the matching **stackable support**, aim at an open existing endpoint, then reopen **K → Walking**. Check the Resume summary. Do not place a new starting support first. Wall/floor attachments and ambiguous or occupied endpoints cannot start a resumed bus. See [Smart Walking](Smart-Walking).

Troubleshooting:27.source: ## Camera Enabled or layout seems unchanged

Troubleshooting:28.source: Native menus hide camera pictures. Resume after changing Enabled. In Camera 2.0, an explicit **All saves** edit includes saved overrides for the current world; choose **This save** for a local exception. Menu settings save immediately, while dragged layout/HUD changes require **Done / Lock**. The shared Cancel action discards pending layout edits. No world reload is required for these settings.

Troubleshooting:31.source:
- What you were trying to build.
- The buildable name.
- The grid size.
- Which Smart feature was active.
- Whether Auto-Connect or Extend was involved.
- Single-player or multiplayer.
- Host or client, if multiplayer.

Water-Extractors:1.source: Water Extractors support horizontal Smart grids, Extend and Restore. Their destinations must remain valid water placements.

Water-Extractors:3.source: Select a Water Extractor and use X/Y grid counts and spacing for a horizontal layout. To Extend, hold the matching extractor and aim at an existing one, then inspect the copied extractor and supported pipe connections before building. See [Extend](Extend) for direction and captured-module controls.

Water-Extractors:4.source: Every child uses the water-depth and terrain checks already applied by Smart scaling. A valid first extractor does not make the other destinations valid. Moving the row onto shallow water or terrain can invalidate it.

The blue previews are unbuilt, and no pipe manifold is shown. Power daisy-chaining is enabled in this example.

Water-Extractors:16.source: After placing the horizontal extractor grid, align a matching row of Pipeline Junction Crosses with its outlets. With Pipe Auto-Connect enabled, inspect the short branches and shared pipeline before building. Keep the entire route clear of the shore and rocks. Normal placement rules and material costs apply.

Water-Extractors:8.source: For a horizontal grid, open **K → Scaling** and enter **Grid X/Y** and **Spacing X/Y**, or use the [wheel and numpad scaling controls](Controls). The runtime HUD reports the grid and active spacing while the world preview shows where every extractor will go. Vertical grid controls do not enable another water layer.

Water-Extractors:9.source: For Extend, aim at a compatible existing extractor with the matching recipe equipped, then adjust the captured row with the Panel or world controls. For a saved Module, use the Restore workflow below. In every case, inspect each destination and its pipe routing before firing the build gun.

Water-Extractors:11.source: Capture the supported Extend layout as a Module, then use **K → Restore → Modules → Load Module** to preview it again. Recheck every destination and the full material cost; Restore still validates the water placements.

Water-Extractors:12.source: Water Extractors remain horizontal: vertical grids and vertical Extend/Restore layers are excluded. Other resource extractors do not gain free-placement scaling from this support. Miners can instead use [Smart Upgrade](Smart-Upgrade) on their original resource nodes.
